issues.legal_issue: A person with no present interest in the property, who expects to obtain a lease only if a specific-performance suit fails, is neither a necessary nor a proper party to that suit when their presence is not needed to adjudicate it.
material_facts: The pending suit sought specific performance of an agreement between the plaintiff and the airport authority.
The proposed additional party was neither a party to that agreement nor a purchaser or lessee of the disputed land, and had no right, title or interest in it.
The proposed party expected that the disputed land might be leased to it if the suit was decided against the plaintiff; the land had not been included in its existing lease.
The plaintiff sought no relief against the proposed party, whose presence was not necessary to pass an effective decree or adjudicate the issues in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The proposed party was neither a necessary nor a proper party, and its application for impleadment was rightly dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order I Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a necessary party is one in whose absence no effective decree can be passed; a proper party is one whose presence enables complete, effective and adequate adjudication of the matters in dispute. A person’s expectation of acquiring an interest after the suit is decided against the plaintiff does not make that person a necessary or proper party. Kasturi v. Iyyamperumal identifies parties to the contract, their legal representatives and transferees as necessary parties in a specific-performance suit, while Sumtibai v. Paras Finance Co. allows a person with a semblance of title or interest to be considered a proper party; the decisions are consistent and turn on their facts. The court’s discretion under Order I Rule 10(2) is judicial and must be exercised according to law, reason and fair play; see also Ramesh Hirachand Kundanmal v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay, Anil Kumar Singh v. Shivnath Mishra and Ramji Dayawala & Sons (P) Ltd. v. Invest Import.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.applicant_not_contract_party_or_transfer: The applicant is neither a party to the contract, that party’s legal representative, nor a transferee of the property from a party to the contract.
predicates.applicant_has_no_present_property_intere: The applicant has no present right, title or interest in the disputed property.
predicates.applicant_expects_interest_only_if_suit_: The applicant expects to acquire an interest in the property only if the suit is decided against the plaintiff.
predicates.applicant_presence_unneeded_for_adjudica: The applicant’s presence is not needed to pass an effective decree or completely adjudicate the issues in the suit.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns an applicant who has no present property interest, expects an interest only if the suit fails, and is not needed for adjudication, the applicant is not added as a party.

issues.legal_issue: A lessee assigned functions over leased airport premises does not acquire authority over land excluded from the lease merely because that land may later be leased to it.
material_facts: The airport authority leased the airport premises to the proposed party and assigned it functions relating to operation, management and development of the demised area.
The disputed parcel was expressly not included in the lease, subject to the outcome of the pending suit.
The proposed party relied on its assigned functions to contend that it should be treated as having stepped into the airport authority’s shoes in relation to the airport premises.
issues.conclusion: The contention had no merit: the lessee’s assigned powers extended only to the area demised to it and did not extend to the disputed land that was not leased to it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12A of the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994 provides that a lessee assigned an airport authority function has the powers of the authority necessary to perform that function in terms of the lease. Those powers do not extend to functions concerning an area that has not been demised or leased to the lessee.

predicates.airport_lessee_claiming_authority_over_d: An airport lessee claims authority over disputed land by relying on functions assigned to it.
predicates.function_assignment_limited_to_leased_ar: The functions assigned to the lessee concern only the area demised to it.
predicates.disputed_area_excluded_from_lease: The disputed area is not included in the lessee’s lease.

issues.definition: If an airport lessee’s assigned functions are limited to its leased area and the disputed land is excluded from that lease, the lessee has no assigned authority over that land.
